results.reason: Issue 2 quotes §14.2: a >50% ownership change is deemed an assignment needing Vantrell's prior written consent. It notes the 30-day termination right, that Schedule 4.4 says 'None', and that the §7.2(c) condition is therefore automatically satisfied without Vantrell's consent.

The response cites §16.1 only for the point that Customer cannot assign without Supplier consent. It never says Vantrell can assign freely, and never raises the risk that the supply contract passes to a competitor or other undesirable party.

Issue 1 calculates the 120-day deadline as September 2, 2026. It notes the SPA is dated September 21, 2026, nineteen days later, so the extension at Extension Pricing is lost unless already exercised.

Issue 3 explains that Side Letter §2 limits Fundamental Reps to §§4.1 and 4.2 and that §11.11 gives the Side Letter priority. Its table shows §§4.3 and 4.12 become subject to the deductible and the 10% cap ($8.45M).

Issue 4 identifies Side Letter §6 (Delaware law, Court of Chancery) as conflicting with SPA §§11.8–11.9 (New York). It notes the Side Letter controls under §11.11 and that this splits forums between indemnification and other disputes.
The response states the cap is 10% of the Purchase Price, $8,450,000.
The response states that SPA §11.11 gives the Side Letter first priority over the SPA.
The response is a memo addressed to [Partner]. Each numbered issue lists the documents and sections, an explanation, why it matters to Halvorsen, and a recommended fix.

The memo opens with an 'Issues Requiring Immediate Client Call' section. Issues are ordered with the deal-critical supply and consent items first, followed by the Side Letter issues, then lesser items.
The response consistently says the deadline has likely passed. Issue 16 raises an open window only as a hypothetical and calls the passed deadline 'the more likely scenario'.
The response states that the Side Letter controls and that Capitalization and Taxes are now capped. It does not claim they remain uncapped.
